column1: # --- R7 controlled-delegatecall (delegatecall-hijack) ---
# NB (R7 Parity - documented NON-FIT for the core R7 detector; Parity is wired under R12 below):
#   fixtures/delegatecall-hijack/b-incident/ParityWalletClone.sol does NOT fire on the principled
#   core R7. R7 flags a delegatecall whose DESTINATION is attacker-settable; Parity's proxy
#   delegatecalls a FIXED (constructor-set immutable) library and forwards
#   arbitrary msg.data, and the bug is an unguarded `initWallet` in that library - a cross-contract
#   fact not statically linkable from the proxy (the immutable `lib` has no in-unit type binding).
#   Flagging "delegatecall forwards msg.data" unconditionally would FP on every legit proxy
#   (EIP-1167/UUPS), breaking the 0-FP-hard rule. So Parity is not an R7 anchor, NOT mislabeled.
#   DECIDED (M 04:38): documented NON-FIT for the static layer (honesty > coverage, as Squid was
#   once a non-fit for R8). The init-hijack class - Parity's unguarded `initWallet` and Audius's
#   re-callable `initialize` both seize an authority role via a delegatecall/proxy - is a shared
#   coverage gap. RESOLVED (owner ship decision 2026-11-14): shipped as R12
#   "unprotected-initializer / init-hijack" (detectors/r12_unprotected_initializer.py), a
#   single-contract predicate that catches the unguarded-initializer ROOT CAUSE directly (R7 stays
#   the delegatecall enabler; the two are complementary, not duplicate - see the RULES.md R12
#   overlap note). Parity is now a wired R12 holdout-vuln below, NOT an R7 anchor; the R7 non-fit stands.

column1: # --- R11 arbitrary-callee drain of a standing approval (NO holdout anchor yet) ---
# R11 currently ships with NO holdout row. Each candidate clone in this class is either removed
# (fabricated) or an honest static-layer non-fit:
#   1. Provenance (owner policy, M 04:42): the ParaSwap + Anyswap clones were fabricated and
#      removed from the corpus - not wired, will not exist.
#   2. Squid (SquidMulticall, 2026-04-07) is a REAL incident but, under variant-B F1 (M 04:53), a
#      documented NON-FIT for the static layer: SquidMulticall.run is a PURE arbitrary executor
#      (`calls[i].target.call(callData)`) that holds NO approval of its own - the fact that victims
#      had approved it is off-contract and not visible in its source. Variant-B F1 fires only when
#      the contract itself spends a standing approval (a custody signal); a bare executor has none,
#      exactly like OZ TimelockController (which must stay silent). Widening F1 back to catch Squid
#      reintroduced FPs on canonical OZ Timelock + Permit2 (A's 78-file probe), so per the pre-agreed
#      plan we hold 0-FP and accept Squid as a non-fit (cf. the R7 Parity non-fit). 0-FP > recall.
#   3. Pennysia (PennysiaSettlementClone, executeSwap(venue, raw calldata) -> transferFrom of a
#      stale approval) is a REAL, verified incident (2026-11-12; track-C manual provenance check,
#      see its wal PROVENANCE.md) and the class-level replacement for the removed ParaSwap slot. It
#      was a CANDIDATE R11-class holdout. FIT-CHECK (D, 2026-11-14): the detector was run on
#      PennysiaSettlementClone.sol under variant B -> 0 findings (does NOT fire). The minimized
#      clone is a PURE arbitrary executor: `executeSwap(address venue, bytes route)` does
#      `venue.call(route)` and the draining `transferFrom` lives in the ATTACKER's calldata, not in
#      the Settlement's own code. So it holds no in-source custody signal (F1-narrow silent) and
#      makes no literal transferFrom of its own (F2 silent) - structurally identical to Squid.
#      Verdict: documented static-layer NON-FIT, NOT wired (honesty > coverage, cf. Squid/Parity).
#      0-FP > recall. (This is the same incident the R3 NB above flags as a Pennysia R11-class
#      holdout rather than an R3 anchor.)
# No R11 candidate passes the static fit-check, so R11's live anchor is the DEV F2 case
# (DrainerKit.drain); R11 ships with no holdout row.
# NB (R4 holdout non-fit, probed and intentionally NOT wired, to avoid a mislabeled anchor):
#   - permit-phishing/anyswap-permit-bypass-victim (AnyswapRouterClone) is a permit-validation

column1: # NB (new-fixture holdout non-fits, probed and intentionally NOT wired, to avoid mislabeled anchors):
#   - create2-metamorphic/tornado-governance-victim under R9: R9 fires ONLY when a contract
#     obtains a code identity (.codehash / codeId) but never enforces it. TornadoGovernanceClone
#     never references a code identity (it stores and delegatecalls a plain address), so R9
#     correctly stays silent - exactly R9's documented scope note on the "pure victim without a
#     code-identity reference". Wiring it under R9 would be a mislabeled FN. Its single-key instant
#     pointer swap is instead captured by R10 above.
#   - upgrade-governance/audius-governance-victim under R10: the Audius drain is a re-callable,
#     unguarded `initialize` that overwrites a `controller` role - NOT a swap of an
#     implementation/module/delegate pointer. R10 fires on a self-performed swap of a live-logic
#     pointer; it does not (and should not) fire on an unprotected initializer that writes a
#     `controller` address (name not in R10's pointer set, no delegatecall of a pointer). The
#     "unprotected / re-callable initializer" mechanism is now covered by its OWN rule R12
#     (shipped 2026-11-14, owner decision), so Audius is wired as an R12 holdout-vuln above. Under
#     R10 it remains an honest skip (different primitive), not a mislabel.
#   - upgrade-governance/wormhole-uninit-impl-victim under R10/R12: a documented static NON-FIT, NOT
#     wired. The subject (WormholeCoreImpl) has a re-init-guarded `initialize` (require(!initialized))
#     and a guardian-gated `submitContractUpgrade` (onlyGuardian), so core R10 (authority-gate) and
#     core R12 (unprotected-initializer) both correctly stay silent. The real flaw is that the
#     IMPLEMENTATION was left uninitialized at deploy (init'd via the proxy) - a deploy-time /
#     cross-contract fact not present in the subject's own guarded source. The syntactic Semgrep R10′
#     used to flag its guarded swap, but that is the "guarded swap != single-key swap" over-fire the
#     R10 authority-gate fix removes, so the scan (core-authoritative) now BLOCKs it. 0-FP > one
#     spurious recall point (cf. the Squid/Parity/Pennysia non-fits; honesty over coverage).
# --- R13 unvalidated-approve-over-pooled-custody (holdout: Hedgey incident vuln + real OZ SafeERC20 safe) ---
